reason: The cited evidence shows that ML potentials can accelerate DFT-level sampling (E1, E2), but none of the passages demonstrate active learning, free-energy integration with MLPs, or application to high-entropy alloy melting. The specific claims about capturing anharmonicity, electron-vibration coupling, and achieving a 10x speedup are unsupported by the provided references.
premises: ML potentials can serve as fast, accurate surrogates for DFT potential energy surfaces
Active learning can efficiently calibrate an MLP with sparse AIMD data
MLP-based free-energy integration can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling
The approach reduces computational cost by at least an order of magnitude vs. explicit AIMD/TOR-TILD
The method is transferable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys
